children: Shares of Comcast and Charter Communications weren't selling off for long.
Comcast stock and Charter Communications rose 1.3% to $24.90 and 4.4% to $139.77, respectively, on Thursday, rebounding after booking declines in the previous session.

Charter Communications and Comcast are the two leading cable internet providers in the U.S. and shares of both companies came under pressure on Wednesday after Comcast Chief Financial Officer Jason Armstrong warned that broadband subscription losses won't recover anytime soon.
"We do think, full year we'll improve our broadband subscriber losses, Armstrong said Wednesday, speaking at Goldman Sachs' communications and technology conference.
"I think quarters are going to now look different within that," Armstrong added. "This particular quarter I don't think we'll improve year-over-year."
Both telecommunications stocks fell, with Comcast dropping 6.6% and Charter stock dropping 8.1%. The moves on Wednesday brought both stocks below their 50-day moving averages.
Part of the issue for Comcast is that the price of fiber optical cables has become "irrational" as demand has skyrocketed, in part due to artificial intelligence and data centers, Armstrong said.

The Comcast executive said that as a result the company has become "incredibly rational in our approach to the market" as prices have soared. Along with those pressures, Armstrong also warned that satellite internet remains a threat to cable providers.
The chief financial officer said that fixed wireless continues to be a pressure on broadband subscriber additions and that "satellite looms out there as a potential threat."
Armstrong said that Comcast isn't yet seeing satellite as a major threat to its business but that there's "no complacency around it."

"I think we'll see it over time and in particular in rural and maybe deep suburban markets, it may be a better option as a competitor than we've faced historically. So that's something we're bracing for," Armstrong said.
Of the satellite internet providers, SpaceX's Starlink has been top of mind for investors and how it could disrupt cable internet providers, as well as Verizon Communications, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

Even with the warnings, shares of Comcast and Charter didn't stay in the red for long and were bouncing back Thursday. It could also be that Comcast has sold off enough, with the stock on pace to snap a four-day losing streak.
Investors, however, shouldn't necessarily trust what they're seeing as both Comcast and Charter remained well below their 200-day moving averages at $26.90 and $180.70, respectively.
